transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only got part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, and it’s been causing problems.
Can you describe what’s going through your mind when this happens? Are you getting distracted by other thoughts or things around you?

Yeah, it’s like they’re talking right to me, and I think I’m listening, but then a minute later I realize I only got pieces of it. I don’t always know where my mind went—it’s just like I missed half of what they said, and then I have to ask them to repeat it. It happens with my supervisor and with my wife, and it’s been causing problems.
Does this kind of difficulty with focusing happen in other situations, like when you're reading, driving, or working on tasks at home?

Yeah, at work especially. On the line, when I’m supposed to do the quality checks, I’ll rush through them and miss small stuff—like a wrong label or a fitting that’s loose. Then my supervisor has to pull me aside because it keeps happening.
Have you had trouble with focus or attention like this for a long time, maybe even going back to when you were in school, or is this something that started more recently?

No, it’s not new. I was like this back when I was a kid too. Teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t sit still, and I’d call out answers or butt into other kids’ work. I was getting in trouble for that even before middle school.
